Checkpoint B

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1
This PR from robin-example adds an on-demand catalog download that runs through the existing export handler, and you are a requested reviewer. The PR has no spec, so it is judged against its own description: code, tests and docs cover the download except for one defect, nothing is deferred, and nothing needs checking after merge.

One problem blocks merging. When the catalog is empty, the download fails with an error instead of returning an empty file, so a user with no catalog entries gets a failure rather than a download (src/export.mjs:24). The test empty catalog download in src/export.test.mjs shows the failure, and a repair that keeps the PR's intended behavior is drafted.

I recommend deliver because the empty-catalog repair is drafted and needs no decision from the author.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair the empty-catalog failure, merge main into the branch if it falls behind, watch the checks, and continue until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review requesting changes, and make no repairs.
3. stop - end the run and leave the PR as it is.

A offers merge/approve/stop, B and C offer deliver/assess/stop, with recommended=1, stop last and the exact hint, and no reject row, overrule hint, note preview or approach-conflict text leaks in. Two small risks are worth guarding in the wording. First, After's second opening sentence now appends "nothing is deferred, and nothing needs checking after merge"; this is close to empty-category accounting, so tell the skill to name only what applies and omit null categories in the opening. Second, B's standing part now mentions the drafted repair and drops Before's CI caveat; this is fine here, but state explicitly that the new reject, overrule and three-section rendering applies only when a validated approach conflict or a failed repair exists, so that a literal "Approach conflicts: none" appendix always yields this unchanged ordinary report and menu. After also drops Before's stray preamble line carrying the full head SHA, which is a slight improvement worth keeping.
